title: Localization of simplicial spaces and the cartesian interval criterion
statement:
Use the Reedy model category, mapping simplicial sets $\operatorname{Map}$, representables $F(n)$ and cartesian internal hom from [lem-coef-simplicial-space-reedy-cartesian], with the model-category axioms of [lem-coef-reedy-model-structure]. Let $f:P\hookrightarrow Q$ be a monomorphism of small simplicial spaces. An $f$-local object means a Reedy fibrant simplicial space $W$ for which $\operatorname{Map}(Q,W)\to\operatorname{Map}(P,W)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence. Call $g:A\to B$ an $f$-local equivalence if $\operatorname{Map}(B,W)\to\operatorname{Map}(A,W)$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for every $f$-local object $W$.

There is a model structure on small simplicial spaces with monomorphisms as cofibrations, $f$-local equivalences as weak equivalences, and $f$-local objects as fibrant objects. It is simplicial for $\operatorname{Map}$: for a monomorphism $i:A\hookrightarrow B$ and a fibration $p:X\to Y$ of this structure, the map $\operatorname{Map}(B,X)\to\operatorname{Map}(A,X)\times_{\operatorname{Map}(A,Y)}\operatorname{Map}(B,Y)$ is a Kan fibration in the sense of [lem-coef-kan-quillen-right-proper], trivial if $i$ is an $f$-local equivalence or $p$ is an $f$-local equivalence. Its fibrations are the maps having the right lifting property against all monomorphisms that are $f$-local equivalences. Every Reedy weak equivalence is an $f$-local equivalence.

Assume, in addition, that $W^{F(1)}$ is $f$-local for every $f$-local object $W$. Then for monomorphisms $i:A\hookrightarrow B$ and $j:C\hookrightarrow D$, their cartesian pushout product
$$(A\times D)\amalg_{A\times C}(B\times C)\longrightarrow B\times D$$
is an $f$-local equivalence whenever either $i$ or $j$ is an $f$-local equivalence.
